title: Classical pro-etale stalks: strict localization and exactness
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, let $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $T_{(\bar t)}=\operatorname{Spec}A^{\mathrm{sh}}_{T,\bar t}$ be the strict localization constructed as the limit of affine pointed etale neighbourhoods in [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Work in the small skeleton and universes of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The canonical map $T_{(\bar t)}\to T$ is an object of this site. For every sheaf $\mathcal H$ of sets or abelian groups on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, evaluation gives an isomorphism
$$\mathcal H(T_{(\bar t)})\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H_{\bar t},$$
natural in $\mathcal H$, where the stalk is the colimit over all pointed weakly etale neighbourhoods [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. The functor $\mathcal H\mapsto\mathcal H_{\bar t}$ on abelian sheaves is exact: it preserves finite limits and finite colimits.

proof.text: Use strictHenselizationResidue, clause (1) of strict-henselization functoriality, with the residue-field embedding induced by the geometric point. It gives a strictly henselian local structure on A = strictHenselizationRing t, a unique compatible residue identification, and the resulting marked closed-point lift l with l followed by j equal to t. Choose an affine open Spec B of T through t. Since every point of Spec A generalizes its closed point, j factors through this open. Apply smallStrictHenselization_indEtale_of_affine_chart to the spectrum preimage of that factorization. The resulting ring map is ind-etale and therefore weakly etale. The affine ring/scheme criterion and composition with the etale open immersion make j weakly etale.

source.place: Tag 0993, lemma-classical-point, proof; Tag 0991, section-points, geometric-stalk paragraph

proof.text: Prove the pointed section construction for any weakly etale X -> Spec A with A strictly henselian local and any field-valued point over the closed point. Choose an affine chart Spec B through the marked point, write a:A->B for its structure map, and localize at the marked prime q. Weak etaleness of localization and composition give A->B_q weakly etale. The equation q contracted to A equals its maximal ideal proves this is a local homomorphism. Olivier makes it bijective. Its ring-equivalence inverse composed with B->B_q defines a section. The marked ring map B->Omega sends elements outside q to units, so it extends to B_q. Composing this extension with A->B_q recovers the base point; cancellation through the ring equivalence proves the section preserves the full field-valued point. For a weakly etale X->S and Spec A->S, apply the section construction to their pullback to obtain the pointed lift.

proof.text: For two pointed lifts a,b:Spec A->X over S, form d=(a,b):Spec A->X times_S X. The weakly etale diagonal X->X times_S X is an instance in Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.WeaklyEtale; it is also the between-objects permanence property applied to these weakly etale S-objects. Equality of the marked points gives a lift of that point through the diagonal. Step 2 lifts d through the diagonal; composing with the two projections forces a=b. Apply existence and uniqueness to every pointed weakly etale neighbourhood of t and wrap the resulting scheme maps as structured arrows. This exhibits the pointed strict localization as an initial object.

proof.text: The opposite of the initial neighbourhood is terminal. For every diagram with values in sets or abelian groups, Mathlib Limits.IsColimit.isIso_ι_app_of_isTerminal makes its canonical colimit leg at this object invertible. NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app proves this for colim.ι itself. Whisker first by restriction to pointed neighbourhoods and then by sheafToPresheaf; thus the exact natural transformations in the statement are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0993, lemma-classical-point, proof; Tag 0991, section-points, geometric-stalk paragraph

proof.text: Every covering sieve on the strict localization contains a pro-etale covering presieve. Express it as a family; joint surjectivity gives a point in one member over the closed point of Spec A. Use its residue-field morphism as the marked field-valued point in the section construction of step 2. The resulting section splits that covering arrow. Sieve downward closure puts the identity in the covering sieve. This argument uses the actual residue field of the selected point and needs no extension of the originally fixed Omega-point.

source.place: Tag 0993, lemma-classical-point, proof; Tag 0991, section-points, geometric-stalk paragraph

proof.text: For an arbitrary abelian presheaf, local injectivity of the sheafification unit gives a covering equalizer sieve when two sections become equal. Step 5 puts the identity in this sieve, proving injectivity on sections at the strict localization. Local surjectivity gives a covering image sieve; again the identity supplies an actual preimage, proving surjectivity. The abelian forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms, so evaluation of the sheafification unit is an isomorphism. The reflective sheafification adjunction then reduces preservation of finite colimits by sheaf evaluation to preservation of pointwise presheaf colimits. Limits of sheaves are sectionwise, so evaluation preserves finite limits. Finally the canonical abelian natural isomorphism from step 4 transfers both preservation properties to the stated stalk functor. This replaces the original image-factorization and cokernel argument by sheafification and the proved reflective-adjunction colimit lemma.
